Inspire Robots RH5MK1 22-DoF hand carries tactile sensing across palm, finger undersides and between fingers, with 0.005 N fingertip force resolution (unveiled IROS 2026 per humanoid.guide).
A Fierce Sensors article says the robotic tactile-sensing market was $224M in 2024, rising to $622M by 2032, citing Verified Research Insights.
China's April 2025 Joint Announcement No. 18 put seven heavy rare earths and terbium- or dysprosium-containing NdFeB magnets under export licensing.
Musk said on Tesla's Q1 2025 call that Optimus production was affected by China's magnet restrictions because Optimus arm actuators use permanent magnets.

claim: NdFeB magnets suit compact high-torque motors; a humanoid uses many small motors and so needs more magnet material than a typical EV, per a Sprott-sponsored analysis (no kg-per-robot figure found; unverified).

Leaderdrive holds 30-40% of China's harmonic reducer market per a J.P. Morgan estimate cited by humanoid.guide; a Odaily newsflash claims over 60%, sourced to a social post and not credible on its own.
Green Harmonic's domestic harmonic reducer share was 33% in 2019, 25% in 2024 and 27.5% the following year, per 36Kr.
Harmonic Drive Systems (Japan) still dominates the premium harmonic-reducer segment, with cheaper Chinese rivals such as Leaderdrive gaining on price.
Schaeffler unveiled at CES 2026 a humanoid actuator integrating a two-stage planetary gearbox, motor, encoder and controller in one compact unit, torque 60-250 Nm.
Schaeffler and Hexagon Robotics agreed on 22 April 2026 to develop and supply rotary actuators for key humanoid joints such as shoulders and elbows.
Schaeffler's portfolio includes ball and planetary roller screw linear actuators for humanoid joints.
Schaeffler's January 2026 investor presentation reports 28 prototype orders from 14 global humanoid OEMs (OEMs not named).
Chinese suppliers accounted for about 96% of shipments of dexterous hands with six or more active DoF in H1 2026, versus about 4% for Western suppliers (market-research summary, not primary).

Dexterous hand actuation falls into three routes per a TrendForce-based report: screw-link, tendon-driven bio-mimetic, and high-sensing; 1X pairs a low-reduction tendon drive with tactile skin, and Tesla pursues a high-precision in-house route not yet proven at mass production.
Unitree Dex5-S is a 22-DoF hand with 22 backdrivable electric motors, one per joint, dual-encoder control, unveiled September 2026 (third-party listing).
Inspire RH56DFX is a 6-DoF hand, with a built-in wrist option adding two DoF, and is reported as among the highest-shipping hands in Inspire's range.
Hesai reports Q2 2026 robotics lidar deliveries of 142,371 units, up 193.4% from 48,531 a year earlier, about 23% of its quarterly lidar shipments.
Hesai's Q4 2025 call named humanoid and quadruped customers including Unitree, Galbot, MagicLab and Vita Dynamics, and expected five-digit annual robotics volumes in 2026.
RoboSense reportedly delivered its one-millionth lidar to a humanoid robot company; date not stated in the source and treated as possibly dated.
CATL supplies cells for the Galbot S1 heavy-duty humanoid (50 kg dual-arm payload), claimed to run more than eight hours with a PPB-level cell failure rate (manufacturer claim).
CATL has commissioned a battery-pack line deploying humanoid robots at its Zhongzhou base; Galbot is reported as the only embodied-AI company CATL has invested in to date.
Qualcomm agreed to acquire PickNik Robotics (MoveIt) at ROSCon, with price undisclosed and closing subject to conditions; reporting differs on whether signed.

Orbbec's Gemini 330-series stereo camera is in shipping humanoids (HONOR's first humanoid, shown at MWC 2026) and has been validated with NVIDIA Jetson Thor; Orbbec's Physis 257g passive stereo module with integrated IMU was introduced at WRC 2026.

Open-source exoskeleton and glove rigs for demonstrations cost about $230 (CDF-Glove) to $500 (HOMIE total hardware), per the papers as summarized.

Commercial data gloves are listed at $2,500-5,000 per pair (Manus Quantum, Rokoko Smartgloves $2,500-4,000) and bimanual ALOHA-style rigs at $20k-25k in a vendor build guide; the guide is internally inconsistent.
Leadshine (China) showed FM-series frameless motors at CES 2026; FM2-8513 is claimed at 7 Nm peak, 326 g, 21.5 Nm/kg torque density, about 70% above an unnamed competitor (company claim).
Allient announced frameless torque and axial-flux motors aimed at robotic and humanoid platforms for Automate 2026 (product announcement only, no performance validation).

NVIDIA's stack splits into Isaac GR00T (robot foundation model, N1.6 latest reported), Newton (open GPU physics engine, Linux Foundation, co-developed with Google DeepMind and Disney Research) and Omniverse (training and synthetic data); announcements mostly date from 2025.
NVIDIA GR00T early adopters named in coverage include Agility Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Mentee Robotics and NEURA Robotics.
ASENSING agreed in March 2026 to supply its automotive-grade IMU 5146 to Galbot's embodied-AI robots for balance control and navigation.
Chinese IMU makers including W-Ibeda, BWSENSING and Shanghai IMU Master sell humanoid-oriented inertial sensors; W-Ibeda states its IMUs go into humanoids for posture and centre-of-gravity sensing.
KVH states fiber-optic gyros and FOG-based IMUs appear in humanoids; vendor-stated, no independent count.
MDT (MultiDimension) launched on 1 July 2026 a TMR magnetic rotary encoder IC for humanoid and quadruped joint sensing, with SPI absolute output at 23-bit.
Renishaw sells robotics encoders (optical ATOM and magnetic AksIM/Orbis); a third-party review says Renishaw owns 50% of RLS, which sells humanoid-oriented magnetic encoders. Netzer not found.

Magnetic encoders are gaining against optical encoders (Renishaw, Heidenhain) in humanoid joints; Chinese magnetic-encoder maker Jingang Tech got Maxchip strategic investment in May 2026 with 24-bit high-precision series.
A HKUST (Guangzhou) lab page calls joint-module heat the limit on long, high-load humanoid operation and says active joint cooling is needed.
quote: Excessive heat generation in joint modules of humanoid robots severely restricts their long-duration and high-load operation.

claim: UT Austin's Human Centered Robotics Lab with Apptronik built a liquid-cooled viscoelastic leg prototype (Draco) that the lab says delivers significantly more mechanical power than convection-cooled legs.
Leaderdrive sold 425,158 harmonic reducers in 2025, up 72% year on year, per a compiled supplier table (secondary).

Nabtesco is the cycloidal (RV) leader, reportedly ~35% of global RV units for articulated robots, planning to double RV capacity by 2026 for humanoid demand; secondary figures not checked against Nabtesco filings.

Cycloidal joints offer high rigidity and shock resistance but are heavier, costlier and less precise than harmonic, which limits their adoption in humanoids; Nabtesco launched compact RVmini and Monocrank series in December 2025 aimed at humanoid joints.
quote: Cycloidal reducer joints offer high rigidity and shock resistance but are heavier, costlier, and less precise, limiting their current market adoption.

claim: Six-axis force-torque supplier list for robots names ATI, Schunk, Sunrise Instruments, Epson and Robotiq; Chinese and Korean humanoid-focused makers include XJCSENSOR (MEMS 6-axis) and Robotous (fingertip-size 6-axis). Humanoid-specific ATI/Robotiq products not found.

Humanoid harness and cable supply is served by custom harness assemblers (e.g. Cloom Tech, announced humanoid wire-harness solutions 13 July 2026) and slip-ring makers for neck and waist joints (Servotecnica, JINPAT, Mercotac, ROTOCON); no public FFC supplier for humanoid joints was found.
Market research puts the humanoid wiring-harness market at US$76.49M in 2025, rising to US$297M by 2032 (vendor-report teaser, not verified).
No public reference design exists for how Boston Dynamics or others carry power and data across humanoid joints; hollow-shaft joint routing is an unresolved design choice in public sources.
